title: RANK 2 the true-hint positive control, and RANK 3 the S-box arm on the r=5 yoyo

certificate.basis: pure measurement; no discrete log, no factor-base relation, no key recovery is claimed. The RANK 2 arm recovers key bytes of a toy 6-round instance, and its correctness is self-certifying in the reported field diagonals_unique_and_correct, which compares the surviving byte against the true key schedule inside the run.

HEADLINE.RANK_3_PLAIN_STATEMENT: The r=5 yoyo signal SURVIVES uniformly random bijective S-boxes. It is therefore NOT specific to the AES S-box, and on the evidence of this campaign so far NOTHING this campaign has found is specific to AES: the r=4 and r=5 counting properties were already reproduced under random bijective S-boxes, and the yoyo -- the last untested signal -- behaves the same way. Every result is a fact about SPN round geometry that AES happens to instantiate.
HEADLINE.RANK_2_positive_control: POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES. The same modified sq_slot binary that returned {0:4} for every single-slot false hint in BATCH-003 rank 4 returns {1:4} -- four diagonals, each with a unique surviving byte equal to the true byte -- when the hint is TRUE. The all-empty regression hypothesis is EXCLUDED: the instrument is demonstrably capable of emitting a non-empty correct result.
HEADLINE.RANK_3_decay_control_statement: All three r=6 arms are DEAD under the frozen rule. The signal is round-limited under the real AES S-box AND under both random S-boxes, which is what a yoyo signal must be, so the object measured at r=5 is the BATCH-002 object and not a non-decaying artifact. The r=6 arms are paired with the r=5 arms on key and trial stream, so rounds is the only variable that changed. This removes an objection; it adds no strength to anything.
HEADLINE.WHAT_CHANGED_IN_SEGMENT_2: The segment-1 S-BOX-INDEPENDENT reading STANDS EXACTLY AS RECORDED, with no upgrade in strength. What changed is that a named defect is closed: the r=6 decay control that segment 1 listed under checks_that_did_not_run has now been run for all three S-boxes and passed, and the random-S-box arms have gained an absolute per-round anchor they previously lacked. No segment-1 number was edited or rescored.

rank_3_sbox_arm.object: E_K^r = ARK_r . SR . SB . [ARK_i . MC . SR . SB]_{i=r-1..1} . ARK_0, round keys = first r+1 of the UNTRUNCATED FIPS-197 AES-128 expansion computed with the SAME S-box the cipher uses. One trial: draw p0; form p1 by re-randomising every byte of every plaintext word in amask (rejecting a draw that leaves an active word unchanged); c0=E(p0), c1=E(p1); swap the ciphertext words in smask between c0 and c1 (a swap whose bytes all already agreed is TRIVIAL and excluded from all counts); q0=D(c0'), q1=D(c1'); d=q0^q1; W = number of plaintext words on which d vanishes; statistic = count of trials with W>=1. Identical to the BATCH-002 yoyo object.

geometry.how_verified: ./yoyo_sbox geom compared byte for byte against BATCH-002/tasks/TASK-20260802-e4fa63/geom.json

implementation.why: the BATCH-002 probe implements AES with AES-NI (_mm_aesenc_si128 / _mm_aesdec_si128), which hardwires the AES S-box in silicon; the S-box cannot be substituted there. src/yoyo_sbox.c is a T-table software AES whose S-box is a run-time parameter, reproducing BATCH-002's conventions, geometry, splitmix64 RNG, thread-seed derivation, key derivation from the arm seed, trivial-swap exclusion and reporting fields; the trial loop is a transcription of BATCH-002's worker() onto byte arrays.

random_sbox_construction.draw: Fisher-Yates shuffle of [0..255] driven by splitmix64 seeded with the recorded seed, with rejection sampling on each index (a 64-bit draw falling in the short tail is rejected), so there is no modulo bias
random_sbox_construction.bijectivity_verified_before_use: the binary checks that every output value occurs exactly once, that all 256 values occur, and that ISBOX[SBOX[x]]==x and SBOX[ISBOX[x]]==x for all x; it exits 4 and refuses to measure otherwise. Independently re-checked in Python: sorted(sbox) == list(range(256)) for both draws.

The red team objected that this is structurally the same defect BATCH-003's red team found for the zero-entry matrices -- a signal claim with no decay control -- reproduced inside the batch convened to repair it. r6_decay_controls_ADDED_IN_SEGMENT_2.design: Same binary (sha256 in runs/yoyo_sbox_binary_sha256_segment2.txt), same geometry, same 2^31 trials, same amask/smask, same analytic null and the same frozen ALIVE/DEAD rule. BATCH-002's r=6 arms used a different key, so this pairing is a stronger decay comparison than the prior batch's.

These controls therefore have LESS resolution than BATCH-002's and can only exclude an excess of roughly 5x or more.

The same modified sq_slot binary that returned {0:4} for every single-slot false hint in BATCH-003 rank 4 returns {1:4} -- four diagonals, each with a unique surviving byte equal to the true byte -- when the hint is TRUE. P3.2 both random mains ALIVE (H-INDEP) o.registered_prior: 50/50 between H-INDEP and H-DEP, frozen before measuring

P3.3 all three structure-destroyed contr.unexpected_observation_recorded_not_disc: Y-R2-sd measured 4 hits against an analytic null of 1.0 (excess 4.0x), OUTSIDE the predicted <=2.5x band. It does not reach the frozen ALIVE bar (one-sided Poisson P(K>=4 | lambda=1) = 0.0190, far above the 1e-6 requirement) and at 2^30 trials a count of 4 against a null of 1 is an ordinary upward Poisson fluctuation. It is recorded because it fell outside a frozen prediction band, and it is a reason to re-run the structure-destroyed controls at higher trial counts before anyone leans on them.

absolute_anchor_for_the_random_sbox_path.why_needed: The segment-1 pin applied the FIPS-197 C.1 known-answer vector at TEN ROUNDS ONLY and only for the real AES S-box (fips197_c1_kat_applicable is false for R1 and R2), and its 5120 encrypt/decrypt round-trips are invariant under any conjugation that enc_r and dec_r share. As recorded in segment 1, the random-S-box arms therefore had NO ABSOLUTE ANCHOR. The red team named this; it is now supplied.
absolute_anchor_for_the_random_sbox_path.what_was_done: an INDEPENDENT plain-Python FIPS-197 implementation (byte-wise SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns, no T-tables, no equivalent-inverse-cipher, no shared code or constants with the C probe) checked against the C probe's enc_r output for EVERY round count r=1..10, under the real AES S-box and under both random S-boxes. This is an absolute per-round anchor and is NOT invariant under a conjugation shared by enc_r and dec_r.
absolute_anchor_for_the_random_sbox_path.reference_implementation: ref_aes.py, plain Python, byte-wise SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns, no T-tables, no equivalent-inverse-cipher, no shared code or constants with src/yoyo_sbox.c

binary_tie_to_the_measuring_binary.purpose: tie the anchor binary yoyo_sbox_v2 to the MEASURING binary yoyo_sbox: identical arm output on short arms, so the per-round anchor validates the code path that produced the measurements
binary_tie_to_the_measuring_binary.v2_diff: src/yoyo_sbox_v2.diff (adds a read-only vec dump mode only)

absolute_anchor_for_the_random_sbox_path.what_it_still_does_not_cover: the anchor checks enc_r at every round count for all three S-boxes. dec_r is still covered only by the round-trip invariant against enc_r; since enc_r is now absolutely anchored, a shared conjugation is excluded, but a decryption-only error that the round-trip cannot see is not separately tested.

confounding_and_arm_level_limits.confound: S-box, KEY and TRIAL STREAM are confounded across the main arms: each arm derives its own AES key from its own seed, so the three r=5 main arms carry three distinct key_hex values and three distinct splitmix64 streams.
confounding_and_arm_level_limits.consequence: This design CANNOT assign an arm-to-arm difference to the S-box rather than to the key or the stream. Concretely: Y-R1-main measured 22 hits and Y-R2-main measured 41 at equal exposure, a difference at two-sided p = 0.0226 under the exact conditional binomial test; this design cannot say whether that is the S-box, the key, the stream or chance.
confounding_and_arm_level_limits.what_IS_free_of_this_confound: the r=5 vs r=6 comparison, because each r=6 arm reuses its r=5 counterpart's seed and arm id, giving an identical key and an identical trial stream with rounds as the only changed variable.
confounding_and_arm_level_limits.what_would_fix_it: replicate each S-box across several independently derived keys and streams at fixed exposure, and/or run the AES S-box and a random S-box under the SAME key. Not run here: budget.
confounding_and_arm_level_limits.recorded_because: the red team raised it and it is a real limit on the arm-to-arm comparison, though it does not bear on the ALIVE/DEAD verdict of any single arm against its own matched null.

what_this_cannot_establish: TOY TIER. This is r=5 of a reduced-round AES-128 permutation with a full 128-bit key schedule, on one implementation, with two random S-box draws and at most 2^31 trials per arm.
Nothing here speaks to full-round or deployed AES, and no comparison to published cryptanalysis is made in either direction.

Two random draws bound very little about the space of 256! bijections. An S-BOX-DEPENDENT reading would say those two particular draws killed the signal, not that the AES S-box is unique; an S-BOX-INDEPENDENT reading would say those two draws preserved it, not that every bijection does.
The structure-destroyed controls ran at 2^30 rather than BATCH-002's 2^32 and can only exclude an excess of roughly 5x or more.
The RANK 2 arm establishes only that the modified sq_slot binary CAN emit a non-empty correct result under a true hint. It does not re-derive BATCH-003's rank-4 slot conclusions.
This session provides no model independence. Nothing here may count toward a closure quorum.
A timeout or resource cap is resource exhaustion and is never negative mathematical evidence.
